books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.about: A Nobel-winning psychologist explains the two systems that drive how we think: the fast, intuitive one and the slow, deliberate one, and the predictable mistakes that happen when we trust the wrong one.

books.title: Mindset
books.author: Carol Dweck
books.about: Why some people grow through failure while others are crushed by it. The difference is whether you believe ability is fixed or can be developed.

books.title: Man's Search for Meaning
books.author: Viktor Frankl
books.about: A psychiatrist who survived Auschwitz describes what kept people alive in the camps, and argues that the main drive in human life is finding meaning.

books.title: Feeling Good
books.author: David D. Burns
books.about: The classic self-help guide to cognitive behavioural therapy: how distorted thoughts create bad moods, and how to talk back to them.

books.title: Influence
books.author: Robert Cialdini
books.about: The six principles of persuasion, including reciprocity, social proof and scarcity, and how to use them honestly and defend against people who misuse them.

books.title: Grit
books.author: Angela Duckworth
books.about: Research showing that passion plus long-term perseverance predicts success better than talent does.

books.title: The Confidence Gap
books.author: Russ Harris
books.about: A practical guide to acting with courage while still feeling fear, based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy.

books.title: The Psychology of Money
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.about: Short stories about how people think about money. Doing well with money is less about knowledge and more about behaviour.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.about: A practical system for building good habits and breaking bad ones through tiny changes that compound over time.

books.title: Deep Work
books.author: Cal Newport
books.about: Why the ability to focus without distraction on hard tasks is rare, valuable and trainable.

books.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
books.author: Stephen Covey
books.about: Principle-centred habits for personal and interpersonal effectiveness, starting from character rather than technique.

books.title: First Things First
books.author: Stephen Covey
books.about: Time management built around what matters most instead of what is most urgent.

books.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
books.author: Dale Carnegie
books.about: The timeless guide to getting along with people: listen, appreciate sincerely, and see things from the other person's side.

books.title: The Noble Qur'an
books.author: Revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
books.about: The word of Allah. These cards hold verses about change, patience and knowledge.

books.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
books.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari
books.about: The most authentic collection of hadith after the Qur'an. Hadith marked with both Bukhari and Muslim are agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh).

books.title: Sahih Muslim
books.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
books.about: The second of the two Sahih collections, known for its careful arrangement of narrations.

books.title: The Forty Hadith
books.author: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi
books.about: Forty-two short hadith that an-Nawawi chose because together they cover the foundations of the religion.

books.title: Jami' at-Tirmidhi
books.author: Imam Muhammad ibn 'Isa at-Tirmidhi
books.about: One of the six major hadith collections, notable for grading each narration.

books.title: Al-Mustadrak
books.author: Imam al-Hakim an-Naysaburi
books.about: A collection of narrations al-Hakim judged to meet the conditions of Bukhari and Muslim but not included by them.

books.title: Hilyat al-Awliya
books.author: Abu Nu'aym al-Asbahani
books.about: A large collection of biographies and sayings of the Companions, the early generations and the righteous scholars.

books.title: Rethinking Positive Thinking
books.author: Gabriele Oettingen
books.about: Twenty years of research showing that positive fantasies alone drain motivation, and the simple WOOP method that turns wishes into action.

books.title: Good Habits, Bad Habits
books.author: Wendy Wood
books.about: The science of the automatic part of your mind: habits form from repeating actions in the same context, and you change them by changing the context, not by relying on willpower.

books.title: The Six Pillars of Self-Esteem
books.author: Nathaniel Branden
books.about: A classic on what self-esteem really is, and the six daily practices that build it, including living consciously and keeping your word to yourself.

books.title: The Power of Your Subconscious Mind
books.author: Joseph Murphy
books.about: A 1963 bestseller that made 'subconscious programming' popular through repetition and visualisation. It's inspiring, but many of its claims are not backed by science, so read it with care.

books.title: Al-Fawa'id
books.author: Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyya
books.about: Short, deep reflections on the heart, the self and the path to Allah by one of the great scholars of the 14th century.

books.title: Never Split the Difference
books.author: Chris Voss
books.about: A former FBI hostage negotiator's techniques for any conversation where something is at stake: listening, labelling emotions, and reaching real agreement.

books.title: Crucial Conversations
books.author: Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, Ron McMillan & Al Switzler
books.about: How to talk when the stakes are high, opinions differ and emotions run strong, without going silent or getting aggressive.

books.title: $100M Offers
books.author: Alex Hormozi
books.about: How to build an offer so valuable that people feel stupid saying no, based on a simple value equation.

books.title: The Mom Test
books.author: Rob Fitzpatrick
books.about: How to talk to customers and find out whether your business idea is any good, even though everyone lies to you to be polite.

books.title: Building a StoryBrand
books.author: Donald Miller
books.about: A simple framework for clear marketing: make the customer the hero of the story, and your brand the guide who helps them win.

books.title: The E-Myth Revisited
books.author: Michael E. Gerber
books.about: Why most small businesses fail, and how to build one that runs on systems instead of on the owner always being there.

books.title: Good to Great
books.author: Jim Collins
books.about: A study of companies that jumped from average to outstanding results and stayed there, and what they did differently.

books.title: Zero to One
books.author: Peter Thiel
books.about: The PayPal co-founder on building something truly new instead of copying what already exists.

books.title: Genius Moves
books.author: Business history
books.about: True stories of smart decisions that built great companies, and the lesson you can take from each one.

books.title: The Life of the Prophet ﷺ
books.author: Ibn Hisham (from Ibn Ishaq)
books.about: The earliest full biography of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, including his years as a trusted merchant before prophethood.

books.title: Bob Proctor's Teachings
books.author: Bob Proctor
books.about: Bob Proctor (1934–2022) taught that results come from your 'paradigm': the habits and beliefs stored in your subconscious mind. Main sources: You Were Born Rich (1984) and his Thinking Into Results programme. Some of his ideas, like the 'law of attraction', are beliefs rather than proven science.

books.title: Jim Rohn's Philosophy
books.author: Jim Rohn
books.about: Jim Rohn (1930–2009) was a business philosopher who taught that success comes from a few simple disciplines repeated every day. Key sources: The Five Major Pieces to the Life Puzzle, The Seasons of Life, and decades of seminars.

books.title: The Strangest Secret
books.author: Earl Nightingale
books.about: A 1956 recorded talk that earned a Gold Record for selling over a million copies. Its core idea: we become what we think about.

books.title: Think and Grow Rich
books.author: Napoleon Hill
books.about: A 1937 classic built on Hill's claim that he studied hundreds of successful people. Historians question some of his stories, but its focus on desire, purpose and persistence still shapes the self-growth world.

books.title: Eat That Frog! & Maximum Achievement
books.author: Brian Tracy
books.about: Brian Tracy's practical system for beating procrastination, setting goals and managing time: do the most important thing first, every day.

cards.b: One part of your mind reacts fast and on instinct. The other is slow, careful and lazy. Most mistakes happen when the fast part answers a question that needed the slow part.
cards.x: Before a big decision today, pause and ask: am I reacting, or thinking?
cards.s: Thinking, Fast and Slow — Daniel Kahneman

cards.t: Losses hurt about twice as much as gains feel good
cards.b: Losing 20 euros stings more than finding 20 euros pleases you. That is why fear of loss often stops people from trying new things that would help them.
cards.x: Name one thing you avoid only because you might lose a little.
cards.s: Thinking, Fast and Slow — Daniel Kahneman

cards.b: The first number you hear, even a random one, pulls your estimate toward it. This is called anchoring, and sellers and negotiators use it on purpose.
cards.x: In your next negotiation, say your number first.
cards.s: Thinking, Fast and Slow — Daniel Kahneman

cards.b: People with a fixed mindset think ability is set at birth, so failure feels like a verdict. People with a growth mindset see ability as something trained, so failure is just feedback.
cards.x: Replace "I'm bad at this" with "I'm not good at this yet."

cards.t: Between what happens and how you respond, there is a gap
cards.b: Frankl survived the Nazi camps and noticed that even there, people kept one freedom: choosing their attitude. That small space before you react is where your strength lives.
cards.x: Next time you get annoyed, count to three before you answer.
cards.s: Man's Search for Meaning — Viktor Frankl

cards.t: A reason to live makes hardship bearable
cards.b: Prisoners who held on to a purpose, a person to return to or work to finish, endured far better than those who lost it. Meaning is fuel.
cards.x: Write one sentence: who or what am I doing this for?
cards.s: Man's Search for Meaning — Viktor Frankl

cards.b: Low mood comes from thinking traps: all-or-nothing thinking, mind reading, fortune telling, labelling yourself. Catching the trap by name weakens it.
cards.x: When you think "they think I'm stupid", ask: what's the actual evidence?

cards.b: Reciprocity is one of the strongest social rules. When you give first, help, share or listen, people naturally want to give back. Also notice when someone uses a small gift to push you.
cards.x: Do one helpful thing today without asking for anything.

cards.t: We copy the crowd when we're unsure
cards.b: When we don't know what to do, we look at what others are doing. That's social proof. Useful, but dangerous: the crowd is often unsure too.
cards.x: Notice one choice this week you made only because others did.

cards.b: Talent times effort gives skill. Skill times effort gives results. Effort shows up in both steps, which is why steady people overtake gifted ones.
cards.x: Pick one skill and put 20 focused minutes into it today.

cards.t: Confidence comes after action, not before
cards.b: Most people wait to feel confident before they act. It works the other way: you act while still nervous, and the feeling of confidence grows from the doing.
cards.x: Do the scary small thing while scared. Let the feeling catch up.

cards.t: Wealth is what you don't see
cards.b: Rich is the car you see someone driving. Wealth is the money they chose not to spend. Real wealth is invisible: savings, freedom and options.
cards.x: Move a small amount to savings today, before you spend anything.
cards.s: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel

cards.b: The hardest money skill is getting the goalpost to stop moving. Without a sense of enough, more never feels like enough.
cards.x: Write down what "enough" looks like for you.
cards.s: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel

cards.b: Tiny improvements look like nothing on a single day. Over a year they compound into something huge, just like small savings do with interest.
cards.x: Choose one habit so small it feels too easy. Start today.

cards.t: Become the type of person, not just hit the goal
cards.b: The deepest habit change is identity. Instead of "I want to read a book", think "I am a reader." Every small action is a vote for who you are becoming.
cards.x: Finish this sentence: I am the kind of person who…

cards.t: Design your space, not your willpower
cards.b: Willpower runs out. Environment doesn't. Put the book on your pillow, the phone in another room. Make good habits obvious and easy, bad ones hidden and hard.
cards.x: Move one temptation out of sight tonight.

cards.t: Stack new habits on old ones
cards.b: Link a new habit to one you already do: "After I [current habit], I will [new habit]." The old habit becomes the reminder for the new one.
cards.x: After I pray Fajr, I will read one page.

cards.b: Missing once is an accident. Missing twice is the start of a new, bad habit. Aim to get back on track fast, not to be perfect.
cards.x: Missed something yesterday? Do a tiny version of it today.

cards.b: Most people are constantly distracted. The ability to concentrate deeply on one hard thing is becoming rare, so it is becoming very valuable.
cards.x: Set a 45-minute timer, phone away, one task only.

cards.t: Switching tasks leaves your mind split
cards.b: When you jump from one task to another, part of your attention stays stuck on the first one. Quick phone checks keep your mind permanently divided.
cards.x: Check messages at two or three set times today, not all day.

cards.t: Work on what you can control
cards.b: Picture two circles: things you worry about, and things you can actually affect. Proactive people spend their energy in the smaller circle, and it slowly grows.
cards.x: List one worry. Then write one action inside your control about it.
cards.s: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People — Stephen Covey

cards.t: Begin with the end in mind
cards.b: Imagine what you want people to say about you at the end of your life. Then check whether your daily schedule is actually moving you there.
cards.x: Write three words you'd want people to use about you.
cards.s: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People — Stephen Covey

cards.b: Most people listen in order to reply. Listen to understand first, and people become much more open to hearing you.
cards.x: In your next disagreement, repeat their point back before giving yours.
cards.s: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People — Stephen Covey

cards.b: If you fill a jar with sand first, the big rocks won't fit. Put the important things into your day first, and the small stuff fits around them.
cards.x: Name tomorrow's one big rock tonight.

cards.t: A person's name is music to them
cards.b: Remembering and using someone's name makes them feel seen. It's one of the easiest ways to be liked and respected.
cards.x: Use the name of the next person you speak with.
cards.s: How to Win Friends and Influence People — Dale Carnegie

cards.b: People enjoy talking with someone who listens well far more than with someone who talks well. Ask about them, and let them speak.
cards.x: In your next conversation, ask two follow-up questions.
cards.s: How to Win Friends and Influence People — Dale Carnegie

cards.b: Criticism makes people defensive, and they rarely change because of it. Understanding and honest appreciation change people far more.
cards.x: Go one full day without complaining. Notice how often you want to.
cards.s: How to Win Friends and Influence People — Dale Carnegie

cards.t: Your future self is a stranger you're working for
cards.b: Small daily choices (sleep, reading, money, prayer) are gifts or debts to the person you'll be in five years. Treat him like someone you care about.
cards.x: Do one thing tonight that future-you will thank you for.

cards.a: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
cards.b: Actions are judged by intentions, and every person gets what they intended.
cards.x: Before studying today, make the intention to benefit yourself and others for Allah's sake.

cards.a: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
cards.b: The strong one is not the one who overpowers others in wrestling. The strong one is he who controls himself when angry.
cards.x: When anger rises, stay silent and change your position.

cards.t: Small and steady beats big and rare
cards.a: أَحَبُّ الأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ
cards.b: The deeds most beloved to Allah are the most consistent ones, even if they are small.
cards.x: Pick one small daily deed: two pages of Qur'an, or one dhikr after every prayer.

cards.a: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ، وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ، احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ
cards.b: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Be eager for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not give up.
cards.x: Choose one beneficial thing and push for it today, with du'a.

cards.t: For the believer, everything is good
cards.a: عَجَبًا لِأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ، إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ
cards.b: How amazing is the affair of the believer: all of it is good. If something good happens he is grateful, and if something bad happens he is patient, and both are good for him.
cards.x: Name one blessing and one hardship today. Thank Allah for the first, be patient with the second.

cards.t: Seeking knowledge is a road to Jannah
cards.a: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
cards.b: Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.
cards.x: Your reading here counts. Renew the intention.

cards.a: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
cards.b: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say something good or remain silent.
cards.x: Before you post or reply today, ask: is this good?

cards.t: Want for others what you want for yourself
cards.a: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
cards.b: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
cards.x: Make du'a today for a friend, asking for the same thing you want.

cards.a: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
cards.b: Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.
cards.x: Skip one piece of gossip or pointless scrolling today.

cards.a: اغْتَنِمْ خَمْسًا قَبْلَ خَمْسٍ: شَبَابَكَ قَبْلَ هَرَمِكَ، وَصِحَّتَكَ قَبْلَ سَقَمِكَ، وَغِنَاكَ قَبْلَ فَقْرِكَ، وَفَرَاغَكَ قَبْلَ شُغْلِكَ، وَحَيَاتَكَ قَبْلَ مَوْتِكَ
cards.b: Take advantage of five before five: your youth before old age, your health before sickness, your wealth before poverty, your free time before you get busy, and your life before death.
cards.x: Which of the five do you have most of right now? Use it.
cards.s: Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim 7846 (graded sahih by al-Albani)

cards.a: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ
cards.b: Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves.
cards.x: Pick one inner thing to change this week: a habit, a thought, a sin.

cards.a: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ۝ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
cards.b: So surely with hardship comes ease. Surely with hardship comes ease. It is said twice, as a promise.
cards.x: Whatever is heavy right now, remember: ease is already attached to it.

cards.a: وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
cards.b: And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge. Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to ask for more of only one thing: knowledge.
cards.x: Say this du'a every time you open this app.

cards.a: الْعِلْمُ مَا نَفَعَ، لَيْسَ الْعِلْمُ مَا حُفِظَ
cards.b: Imam ash-Shafi'i said: knowledge is what benefits, not what is merely memorised. Reading is only the start; acting on it is the point.
cards.x: From today's cards, act on just one.

cards.t: You are only a number of days
cards.a: يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ، إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ أَيَّامٌ، كُلَّمَا ذَهَبَ يَوْمٌ ذَهَبَ بَعْضُكَ
cards.b: Al-Hasan al-Basri said: O son of Adam, you are nothing but days. Every time a day passes, a part of you is gone.
cards.x: Make today count for one good thing.

cards.a: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
cards.b: The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
cards.x: Learn the meaning of one ayah today and share it with someone.

cards.a: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَأَمْوَالِكُمْ، وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
cards.b: Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
cards.x: Fix one hidden thing between you and Allah today.

cards.a: يَسِّرُوا وَلَا تُعَسِّرُوا، وَبَشِّرُوا وَلَا تُنَفِّرُوا
cards.b: Make things easy and do not make them difficult. Give good news and do not drive people away.
cards.x: Be the easy one today: at home, at work, in the masjid.

cards.a: كُنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّكَ غَرِيبٌ أَوْ عَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ
cards.b: The Prophet ﷺ took Ibn 'Umar by the shoulder and said: Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveller.
cards.x: Before an argument or a purchase, ask: will this matter on the journey?

cards.t: Follow a bad deed with a good one
cards.a: اتَّقِ اللَّهَ حَيْثُمَا كُنْتَ، وَأَتْبِعِ السَّيِّئَةَ الْحَسَنَةَ تَمْحُهَا، وَخَالِقِ النَّاسَ بِخُلُقٍ حَسَنٍ
cards.b: Fear Allah wherever you are, follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will wipe it out, and treat people with good character.
cards.x: Made a mistake today? Follow it right away with a good deed.

cards.a: تَبَسُّمُكَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيكَ لَكَ صَدَقَةٌ
cards.b: Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you.
cards.x: Smile at three people today.

cards.b: In Oettingen's studies, people who only fantasised about a great outcome put in less effort and achieved less. The mind treats the dream as if you've already arrived, so your drive drops.
cards.x: Keep the dream, but always pair it with the obstacle in your way.

cards.t: WOOP: turn a wish into a plan
cards.b: Four steps, five minutes. Close your eyes for the middle two.
steps: Wish: one wish for the next 4 weeks that's challenging but doable
Outcome: imagine the best result. How does it feel?
Obstacle: find the main obstacle inside you, like a habit, feeling or belief
Plan: write "If [obstacle], then I will [action]."
cards.x: WOOP one goal tonight before you sleep.

cards.b: "I'll exercise more" rarely works. "If it's 7am on Monday, then I put on my shoes and walk" works much better. A review of 94 studies found these if-then plans had a strong effect on reaching goals.
cards.x: Turn one goal into: If [time or place], then I will [action].
cards.s: Research by Peter Gollwitzer & Paschal Sheeran (2006)

cards.t: Specific, hard goals beat "do your best"
cards.b: Decades of research by Locke and Latham show that clear, challenging goals lead to better performance than vague ones. "Do your best" gives your mind nothing to aim at.
cards.x: Rewrite one vague goal with a number and a date.
cards.s: Goal-setting theory — Edwin Locke & Gary Latham

cards.a: اعْقِلْهَا وَتَوَكَّلْ
cards.b: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ whether he should tie his camel and trust Allah, or leave it loose and trust. He said: Tie it, and trust. Every goal needs both effort and tawakkul.
cards.x: Do your part on one goal today, then leave the result to Allah.

cards.t: Your autopilot runs much of your day
cards.b: In Wendy Wood's diary studies, about 43% of what people did each day was done out of habit, often while thinking about something else. To change your life, change what your autopilot does.
cards.x: List three things you do daily without thinking. Is each one helping you?
cards.s: Good Habits, Bad Habits — Wendy Wood

cards.t: Change the cue, not your willpower
cards.b: Habits are triggered by context: a place, a time, the people around you, what you just did. People who seem to have great self-control mostly avoid temptation instead of fighting it.
cards.x: Change one cue: charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight.
cards.s: Good Habits, Bad Habits — Wendy Wood

cards.t: How a thought becomes a habit
cards.a: دَافِعِ الْخَطْرَةَ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ صَارَتْ فِكْرَةً
cards.b: Ibn al-Qayyim said: push away the passing thought, or it becomes an idea. Then he described the whole chain. Stop it early, because each step is harder to stop than the one before.
steps: A passing thought (khatrah)
becomes an idea (fikrah)
becomes a desire (shahwah)
becomes a firm intention ('azimah)
becomes an action (fi'l)
becomes a habit ('adah), which is hard to leave
cards.x: Catch one bad thought today at step 1, before it becomes an idea.

cards.t: Picture the process, not just the prize
cards.b: In a UCLA study, students who imagined themselves studying did better on their exam than students who only imagined getting a top grade. Visualise the steps, not just the finish line.
cards.x: Spend one minute picturing exactly how you'll do tomorrow's hardest task.
cards.s: Research by Lien Pham & Shelley Taylor (UCLA, 1999)

cards.b: In one study, people with low self-esteem felt worse after repeating "I am a lovable person". When a statement feels false, the mind argues back. Saying what you're working on, or writing about values that matter to you, works better.
cards.x: Swap "I am confident" for "I'm learning to speak up, one step at a time."
cards.s: Research by Joanne Wood and colleagues (2009)

cards.b: Murphy taught that what you think about before sleep sinks into the subconscious. Science doesn't support 'programming' this way, but reviewing what you want to learn before sleep does help memory. The Sunnah also gives us adhkar for exactly this moment.
cards.x: Tonight, read your main goal once, then say your evening adhkar.
cards.s: The Power of Your Subconscious Mind — Joseph Murphy

cards.t: Confidence is a promise you keep to yourself
cards.b: Branden called it personal integrity: when your actions match your words, you learn to trust yourself. Every broken promise to yourself chips away at self-esteem.
cards.x: Make one small promise to yourself today, and keep it.
cards.s: The Six Pillars of Self-Esteem — Nathaniel Branden

cards.b: Repeat the last one to three words someone said, in a curious tone. It makes people feel heard and keeps them talking, so you learn more.
cards.x: Them: "It's been a crazy week." You: "A crazy week?"
cards.s: Never Split the Difference — Chris Voss

cards.b: Labelling an emotion calms it down. Start with "It seems like…" or "It sounds like…", then stay quiet and let them answer.
cards.x: Try: "It sounds like you're under a lot of pressure."
cards.s: Never Split the Difference — Chris Voss

cards.b: "You're right" often means "please stop talking". "That's right" means they feel truly understood. Summarise their view so well that they say it.
cards.x: Before you argue, summarise their position until they say "that's right".
cards.s: Never Split the Difference — Chris Voss

cards.t: When it gets heated, make it safe
cards.b: When people go silent or get aggressive, it's because they don't feel safe. Step out of the topic and restore safety: show that you share a goal and that you respect them.
cards.x: Say: "I'm not trying to win this. I want us both to be happy with the result."
cards.s: Crucial Conversations — Patterson, Grenny, McMillan & Switzler

cards.b: Five steps to speak your mind without starting a fight.
steps: Share your facts: what you saw or heard
Tell your story: what you think it means
Ask for their side
Talk tentatively: "I'm starting to wonder if…"
Encourage them to disagree
cards.x: Use STATE in the next awkward conversation you've been avoiding.
cards.s: Crucial Conversations — Patterson, Grenny, McMillan & Switzler

cards.a: فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا لَّعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ
cards.b: Allah sent Musa and Harun to the worst tyrant on earth and told them: speak to him gently, that perhaps he may remember or fear Allah. If gentleness was the method for Pharaoh, it's the method for everyone.
cards.x: Soften your tone in your next disagreement.

cards.a: وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ
cards.b: The Prophet ﷺ said: A good word is charity. Encouragement, thanks and kind advice all count.
cards.x: Send one sincere message of thanks today.

cards.b: To build a habit, make it:
steps: Obvious: a clear cue you can't miss
Attractive: pair it with something you enjoy
Easy: shrink it to two minutes
Satisfying: give yourself an instant reward
cards.x: To break a bad habit, flip them: invisible, unattractive, hard, unsatisfying.

cards.b: People judge your offer on four things. Push the first two up and the last two down.
steps: Dream outcome: how big is the result?
Likelihood: how sure are they it will work?
Time delay: how fast do they get it?
Effort & sacrifice: how easy is it for them?
cards.x: Pick one offer you have. Which of the four could you improve this week?

cards.b: A great offer to the wrong market fails, while an average offer to a desperate market sells. Choose people with a painful problem, money to spend, who are easy to reach, in a growing market.
cards.x: Who has a painful problem you could solve with your skills?

cards.t: Make them feel stupid saying no
cards.b: Don't compete on price. Stack so much value (bonuses, guarantees, speed, support) that nobody can compare your offer to anyone else's.
cards.x: Add one guarantee or bonus that removes your customer's biggest fear.

cards.t: Ask questions nobody can lie to
cards.b: Everyone says your idea is great to be polite, even your mum. These rules get you the truth:
steps: Talk about their life, not your idea
Ask about specific things they did in the past, not what they would do
Talk less, listen more
cards.x: Ask: "When did you last have this problem? What did you do about it?"

cards.t: Compliments are worthless, commitments are gold
cards.b: "That sounds cool" means nothing. Real interest shows up as commitment: their time (a meeting), their reputation (an introduction) or their money (a pre-order).
cards.x: Next time someone likes your idea, ask for a small commitment.

cards.t: Your customer is the hero, not you
cards.b: Most marketing talks about the company, and customers don't care. Make them the hero with a problem, and make yourself the wise guide with a plan.
cards.x: Rewrite your bio or post so the first sentence is about their problem.

cards.b: Every clear marketing message follows this story:
steps: A character (your customer) wants something
They have a problem
They meet a guide (you)
Who gives them a plan
And calls them to action
That helps them avoid failure
And ends in success
cards.x: Write one line for each step about your skill or product.

cards.t: Work on your business, not just in it
cards.b: Most small businesses are started by a skilled worker who ends up trapped doing all the work. The owner's real job is to build the system that does the work.
cards.x: Write down one task you repeat often, step by step, so someone else could do it.
cards.s: The E-Myth Revisited — Michael E. Gerber

cards.t: Build it like you'll franchise it
cards.b: Imagine your business will be copied 5,000 times. Then everything must run on clear systems, not on you being there. Even if you never franchise, it makes the business calm and sellable.
cards.x: Ask yourself: could my business run for one week without me?
cards.s: The E-Myth Revisited — Michael E. Gerber

cards.b: Great companies got the right people on the bus, and the wrong people off, before deciding where to drive. With the right people, the direction is easier to find.
cards.x: Who are the three people you most want on your team or in your circle?

cards.b: The great companies focused only on where three circles overlap:
steps: What you can be the best in the world at
What drives your income best
What you are deeply passionate about
cards.x: Draw the three circles for yourself tonight.

cards.b: Every big company started by owning a small market. Amazon started with books, Facebook with one university. Be the best for a small group first, then expand.
cards.x: Name the smallest group you could become the go-to person for.

cards.t: What do you know that others don't?
cards.b: Thiel's favourite question: what important truth do very few people agree with you on? Great businesses are built on a secret that others missed.
cards.x: Write one honest answer to that question.

cards.t: Toyota let any worker stop the factory
cards.b: On Toyota's lines, any worker could pull the andon cord to stop production when they spotted a problem. Others thought it was crazy. It forced problems to be fixed at the source, and Toyota's quality became legendary.
cards.x: Fix problems the moment you see them, before they grow.

cards.t: McDonald's: cut the menu, win the market
cards.b: In 1948 the McDonald brothers cut their menu to nine items and designed their kitchen like a factory line, even drawing it in chalk on a tennis court to test it. Food came out in seconds. Simplicity scaled.
cards.x: What could you remove to make your product faster or simpler?
cards.s: The McDonald brothers' Speedee Service System, 1948

cards.t: Know what business you're really in
cards.b: Ray Kroc's company struggled to make money from franchise fees. His finance chief Harry Sonneborn saw the real opportunity: buy the land and lease it to franchisees. McDonald's became one of the world's biggest property owners.
cards.x: Ask: where does the real money in my field actually come from?
cards.s: McDonald's history — Ray Kroc & Harry Sonneborn

cards.b: Nintendo started in 1889 making playing cards. Designer Gunpei Yokoi's rule was "lateral thinking with withered technology": use cheap, proven tech in new ways. The Game Boy was weaker than its rivals, but cheaper, tougher and easier on batteries, and it won.
cards.x: What simple tool you already have could you use in a new way?

cards.b: Big retailers ignored small towns. Sam Walton opened stores there, won those markets completely, then grew outward. He was also famous for walking competitors' stores and taking notes on what they did well.
cards.x: Find a customer group the big players ignore.

cards.t: Apple saved itself by saying no
cards.b: When Steve Jobs returned in 1997, Apple was close to bankruptcy and sold dozens of products. He cut them to four: a desktop and a laptop for consumers, and the same for professionals. Focus brought Apple back.
cards.x: List what you're working on. What would you cut to focus on the best two?

cards.t: Amazon writes the press release first
cards.b: Before building a new product, Amazon teams write the press release announcing it, plus answers to customers' likely questions. If the announcement isn't exciting, they don't build it. They call it working backwards.
cards.x: Write a five-line announcement for your idea before you build anything.

cards.a: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فِي أَهْلِكَ وَمَالِكَ، دُلُّونِي عَلَى السُّوقِ
cards.b: When Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf arrived in Madinah with nothing, his Ansari brother offered him half his wealth. He replied: May Allah bless your family and wealth for you. Show me the market. He became one of the richest Companions through trade.
cards.x: Instead of waiting for help, ask: where is my market?

cards.b: Khadijah (RA) was a successful merchant who hired men to trade her goods. She hired Muhammad ﷺ, known as al-Amin, the trustworthy, to take her caravan to Syria. His honesty and the profit he brought impressed her, and she later proposed marriage to him.
cards.x: Build a name for trustworthiness. It's your best marketing.

cards.t: Honesty brings barakah to a deal
cards.a: فَإِنْ صَدَقَا وَبَيَّنَا بُورِكَ لَهُمَا فِي بَيْعِهِمَا، وَإِنْ كَتَمَا وَكَذَبَا مُحِقَتْ بَرَكَةُ بَيْعِهِمَا
cards.b: If the buyer and seller are truthful and make things clear, their deal is blessed. If they hide things and lie, the blessing of their deal is wiped out.
cards.x: Tell a customer one honest limitation of your product or service.

cards.t: Allah loves work done with excellence
cards.a: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ إِذَا عَمِلَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَمَلًا أَنْ يُتْقِنَهُ
cards.b: Allah loves that when one of you does a job, he does it with excellence (itqan). Quality work is a form of worship.
cards.x: Do one task today 10% better than it needs to be.
cards.s: Al-Bayhaqi, Shu'ab al-Iman · hasan (al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami' 1880)

cards.t: After prayer, go seek your provision
cards.a: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلَاةُ فَانتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ
cards.b: And when the prayer is finished, spread out in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah. Worship and work go together.
cards.x: After Jumu'ah this week, do one task that grows your income.

cards.b: A paradigm is a set of habits and beliefs stored in your subconscious mind. Proctor taught that it controls your results more than your knowledge does. That's why people know what to do but still don't do it.
cards.x: Name one result you keep getting. What belief might be behind it?

cards.b: Proctor said a paradigm changes in two ways: an emotional shock, or spaced repetition of a new idea. You can't plan a shock, so repeat the new idea daily until it feels normal.
cards.x: Pick one new belief. Read it aloud morning and night for 30 days.

cards.t: The stick person: how results happen
cards.b: Proctor drew a simple figure to explain where results come from:
steps: Your conscious mind chooses thoughts
Repeated thoughts are stored in your subconscious
Your subconscious drives your feelings
Feelings drive your actions
Actions produce your results
cards.x: To change a result, start at the top: choose a new thought on purpose.

cards.t: Write a goal card and carry it
cards.b: Write your main goal on a small card in the present tense, as if it's already done: "I am so happy and grateful now that…". Carry it and read it several times a day.
cards.x: Write your goal card today and keep it in your wallet or phone case.
cards.s: Bob Proctor · You Were Born Rich

cards.t: Set a goal that scares and excites you
cards.b: Proctor taught that a real goal should sit just beyond your current ability. If you already know exactly how to reach it, it won't force you to grow.
cards.x: Look at your main goal. Does it make you a little nervous? If not, raise it.

cards.b: When you move toward a big goal, your old paradigm fights back with fear and doubt. Proctor called this the terror barrier. Most people turn back there. Those who push through find freedom on the other side.
cards.x: When the fear comes, name it, and take one small step anyway.

cards.b: Proctor said: decide what you want, and the way will appear as you move. Waiting to see the full plan before you commit keeps most people stuck forever.
cards.x: Commit to one goal today without knowing every step. Write it down.
cards.s: Bob Proctor · You Were Born Rich

cards.b: Besides your five senses, Proctor taught six mental tools that grow stronger with use:
steps: Imagination: see what isn't there yet
Will: hold your focus on one thing
Perception: choose how you see a situation
Reason: think things through
Intuition: pick up on what isn't said
Memory: strengthen it by using it
cards.x: Train one today: spend 5 minutes using your imagination on your goal.

cards.b: Proctor taught that your income is tied to three things: the need for what you do, your ability to do it, and how hard it would be to replace you. To earn more, grow all three.
cards.x: Which of the three could you raise this year?
cards.s: Bob Proctor · You Were Born Rich

cards.t: Build more than one source of income
cards.b: Most people trade hours for money, and hours run out. Proctor taught that wealthy people build several income sources that don't all depend on their time.
cards.x: Brainstorm one income idea that doesn't need your time every hour.
cards.s: Bob Proctor · You Were Born Rich

cards.t: Study one great book for years
cards.b: Proctor read Think and Grow Rich almost every day for over 50 years, and said he understood it better each time. Going deep with one great book beats skimming hundreds.
cards.x: Pick the book that changed you most. Reread one chapter this week.

cards.a: لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ
cards.b: Proctor began every goal statement with "I am so happy and grateful now that…". Gratitude puts you in a state where action is easier. The Qur'an goes further: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.
cards.x: Write three things you're grateful for before you check your phone tomorrow.

cards.b: Proctor said most people don't really think. They react to what's around them. Real thinking means building ideas in your own mind, on purpose, with no distractions.
cards.x: Spend 15 minutes with a notebook today on one problem. No phone.

cards.t: Act like the person you're becoming
cards.b: Proctor taught: see yourself already living your goal, then act like that person now, in how you speak, dress and spend your time.
cards.x: Ask: how would the person who reached my goal spend tomorrow morning? Do that.
cards.s: Bob Proctor · You Were Born Rich

cards.t: The law of attraction: a belief, not science
cards.b: Proctor famously taught the 'law of attraction': that your thoughts and 'vibration' attract matching results. There's no scientific evidence for that part. What research does support is clear goals, focus and repeated action.
cards.x: Keep the vision and the focus. Add the action, and the du'a.
cards.s: Bob Proctor · with a science check

cards.t: Work harder on yourself than on your job
cards.b: Rohn's most famous line. Your job pays you for your time, but working on yourself makes you more valuable, and value is what gets paid.
cards.x: Spend 30 minutes today on a skill that makes you more valuable.

cards.t: The five pieces of the life puzzle
cards.b: Rohn taught that every life is built from five pieces:
steps: Philosophy: what you know and believe
Attitude: how you feel about it
Activity: what you do about it
Results: what you get from the activity
Lifestyle: how you design your life with the results
cards.x: Which piece is weakest for you right now?
cards.s: Jim Rohn · The Five Major Pieces to the Life Puzzle

cards.b: Rohn taught that everyone suffers one of two pains: the pain of discipline or the pain of regret. Discipline weighs ounces. Regret weighs tons.
cards.x: Choose one small discipline today that saves you a big regret later.

cards.t: Success is a few simple disciplines
cards.b: Rohn said success is a few simple disciplines practised every day, and failure is a few small errors in judgement repeated every day. Neither shows up in a single day.
cards.x: Name one small daily error you could stop this week.

cards.b: Hard times come to everyone, like winter. Rohn's advice: don't wish it were easier, wish you were better. Don't wish for fewer problems, wish for more skills.
cards.x: In your current difficulty, which skill would help you handle it better?
cards.s: Jim Rohn · The Seasons of Life

cards.b: Rohn compared life to the seasons of a farm:
steps: Winter: hard times come. Don't wish them away, grow stronger
Spring: opportunity. Plant something while you can
Summer: protect what you planted from the weeds
Autumn: harvest what you planted, without complaint or apology
cards.x: Which season are you in? What should you be doing in it?
cards.s: Jim Rohn · The Seasons of Life

cards.t: You become like the people around you
cards.a: الرَّجُلُ عَلَى دِينِ خَلِيلِهِ، فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْ يُخَالِلُ
cards.b: Rohn is credited with the idea that you're the average of the five people you spend the most time with. The Prophet ﷺ said it 1,400 years earlier: A person is upon the way of his close friend, so let each of you look at whom he befriends.
cards.x: List your five closest people. Who lifts you, and who pulls you down?
cards.s: Jim Rohn · Sunan Abi Dawud 4833, Tirmidhi 2378 (hasan)

cards.b: Rohn taught that wages can make you a living, but profits can make you a fortune. Keep your job if you need it, but start something on the side that earns a profit.
cards.x: What could you sell this month, even something small, to earn your first profit?

cards.b: Rohn's plan for every pay cheque, however small:
steps: Live on 70%
Give 10% in charity
Invest 10% to build capital (choose halal options)
Save 10% for emergencies and opportunities
cards.x: Next pay day, split your money this way, even with small amounts.

cards.t: Read every day, write it down
cards.b: Rohn said the book you don't read can't help you, and an idea you don't write down is soon gone. He kept journals of everything he learned for decades.
cards.x: Start a Hikmah journal: write down one idea a day from this app.

cards.t: Run the day, or the day runs you
cards.b: Rohn taught: don't start a day until it's planned. Without a plan, other people's priorities fill your time.
cards.x: Tonight, write tomorrow's plan in five lines.

cards.b: Rohn taught that when your reasons are strong enough, the how gets easier. Weak reasons give up at the first obstacle.
cards.x: Write five reasons why your main goal matters to you.

cards.t: Be happy now, while you pursue more
cards.b: Rohn taught to be happy with what you have while you work for what you want. This is close to qana'ah: being content with Allah's provision without giving up effort.
cards.x: Thank Allah for one thing you have before you think about what you want.

cards.b: Rohn advised joining a group where the expectations are high, because you won't grow where everything is easy.
cards.x: Find one class, group or mentor that will stretch you.

cards.t: Nobody can do your push-ups for you
cards.b: Rohn liked to say you can't hire someone to do your push-ups for you. Reading, discipline, prayer and growth are things only you can do.
cards.x: Do one thing today for your growth that only you can do.

cards.t: We become what we think about
cards.b: This was Nightingale's 'strangest secret'. A person thinking about a clear, worthy goal moves toward it. A person with no goal drifts wherever life pushes them.
cards.x: What have you thought about most today? Is it moving you toward your goal?

cards.t: Success is moving toward a worthy goal
cards.b: Nightingale defined success as "the progressive realisation of a worthy ideal". It isn't only the finish line. Anyone moving step by step toward a worthy goal is already succeeding.
cards.x: Write your worthy ideal in one sentence.

cards.t: One hour a day builds an expert
cards.b: Nightingale taught that one hour a day of study in your field would put you near the top of it within about five years.
cards.x: Block one hour a day this week to study your field.

cards.b: Nightingale said not to give up on a dream because of how long it will take. The years are going to pass either way. The only question is whether they bring you closer.
cards.x: Start the long goal you've been delaying. Day one is today.

cards.b: At the end of The Strangest Secret, Nightingale sets a challenge. Write your goal on a card and think about it often. For 30 days, don't let negative thoughts take over. If you slip, start the 30 days again.
cards.x: Start your 30 days today.

cards.t: A burning desire, not a wish
cards.b: Hill taught that every achievement starts with a desire so strong it becomes an obsession. Wishing is passive. Desire makes you act.
cards.x: Turn one wish into a desire: what are you willing to give for it?
cards.s: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill

cards.t: Hill's six steps to a big goal
cards.b: Hill's method, for money or any big goal:
steps: Decide exactly what you want
Decide what you'll give in return
Set a definite date
Make a plan and start at once, ready or not
Write it all in one clear statement
Read it aloud twice a day, morning and night
cards.x: Write your statement tonight.
cards.s: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill

cards.a: وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ
cards.b: Hill taught that two or more people working together toward a definite goal create more than each could alone. The Qur'an commands the same: cooperate in goodness and piety.
cards.x: Invite two driven friends to meet weekly and push each other's goals.
cards.s: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill · Qur'an 5:2

cards.b: Hill wrote that every adversity and failure carries the seed of an equal or greater benefit. Your job is to look for the seed.
cards.x: Write down one past setback, and one good thing that came from it.
cards.s: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill

cards.b: Hill tells of R.U. Darby, who stopped digging for gold and sold his machine for scrap. The buyer hired an expert and found gold just three feet further down. Persistence is what most people lack.
cards.x: What did you give up on too early? Try once more.
cards.s: Think and Grow Rich — Napoleon Hill

cards.b: Do your hardest, most important task first thing in the morning, and the rest of the day feels easy. If you have two frogs, eat the ugliest one first.
cards.x: Name tomorrow's frog tonight.

cards.b: Before you start, label every task on your list:
steps: A: must do, serious consequences if not
B: should do, mild consequences
C: nice to do, no real consequences
D: delegate it to someone else
E: eliminate it completely
cards.x: Don't touch a B task while an A task is undone.

cards.b: About 20% of your tasks create 80% of your results. Find the few that matter most and give them your best energy.
cards.x: Circle the two tasks on today's list that matter most.

cards.b: Tracy recommends writing your top 10 goals each morning in the present tense, without looking at yesterday's list. Repetition keeps them at the front of your mind.
cards.x: Tomorrow morning, write 10 goals as "I…" statements.

cards.t: Invest 3% of your income in yourself
cards.b: Tracy advises putting 3% of your income into books, courses and learning. Your ability to earn is your most valuable asset, so keep upgrading it.
cards.x: Work out 3% of your income. What will you learn with it this month?

cards.t: Turn your commute into a university
cards.b: Tracy suggests listening to audio lessons while you drive or travel. Over a year, those hours add up to the time of a university course.
cards.x: Put on an audiobook or lecture for your next commute.

cards.t: Allah is as you expect Him to be
cards.a: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي
cards.b: Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me. This is the real positive mindset: expect good from Allah, then work for it.
cards.x: Make du'a today for your biggest goal, expecting Allah to answer.

cards.t: You get what you strive for
cards.a: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
cards.b: And that a person will have nothing except what he strives for. Vision and positive thinking matter, but this verse makes it clear: the striving is what counts.
cards.x: Turn today's best idea into one real action before sunset.
